decks.name: LeetCode #973 - K Closest Points to Origin
decks.description: Find k closest points to origin based on Euclidean distance

cards.question: K Closest Points to Origin: Given an array of points where points[i] = [xi, yi] represents a point on the X-Y plane and an integer k, return the k closest points to the origin (0, 0). The distance between two points on the X-Y plane is the Euclidean distance (i.e., √((x1 - x2)² + (y1 - y2)²)). You may return the answer in any order. The answer is guaranteed to be unique (except for the order that it is in).

solutions.name: Sorting
solutions.explanation: Sort all points by their Euclidean distance from origin (x²+y²), then return first k points. Simple approach but sorts entire array even though we only need k elements. No need to compute square root since relative ordering preserved. O(n log n) time complexity. Space O(1) or O(n) depending on sort implementation.

solutions.name: Min-Heap
solutions.explanation: Build min-heap containing all points with distances, then pop k times to get k closest. Create array of [distance, x, y] for each point, heapify in O(n), then pop k times at O(log n) each. Total O(k log n) after heapify. Better than sorting when k is small. Space O(n) to store heap. Not optimal because maintains all n points in heap.

solutions.name: Max Heap
solutions.explanation: Maintain max-heap of size k containing k closest points seen so far. Iterate through all points, add to heap, if size exceeds k pop farthest (max). Heap always contains k closest points. Negate distances to simulate max-heap in Python. O(n log k) time as n insertions with O(log k) heap operations. Space O(k) for heap. Most efficient heap approach.

solutions.name: Quick Select
solutions.explanation: Use partition-based selection similar to quicksort to find kth smallest distance. Partition array around pivot, if pivot index equals k we have k closest points in left partition. If pivot < k, search right partition; if pivot > k, search left partition. Average O(n) time with single pass through data. Worst case O(n²) with poor pivot choices. Space O(1) with in-place partitioning. Most efficient average case solution.
